title: Coordinate Reference Systems & Projections
interviewAnswer: A CRS defines how coordinates map to Earth. Longitude/latitude is angular; projected CRSs map locations to a plane for meaningful distance/area calculations over a suitable region.
why: CRS mistakes can produce plausible-looking but numerically wrong spatial analysis.
intuition: One degree of longitude is not the same ground distance everywhere.
deepDive: Every map projection preserves some properties and distorts others; choose based on spatial extent and measurement needs.
commonMistakes: Computing kilometer distances directly in degrees.
Assigning a CRS label instead of transforming coordinates.
production: Store CRS metadata and make transformations explicit/reproducible.
workedExample: Before buffering points by 5 km, reproject EPSG:4326 coordinates to an appropriate projected CRS.
